messages:
Maya: FYI rolling kernel upgrade to 6.4 landed in eu-west3 ~2h ago. We're getting a wave of P4 hosts failing driver probe and a bunch of NCCL handshakes timing out. Can we triage?

Jin: Seeing deferred probe + nv-host OOM on p4-14-12 and a couple of p4-32s. dmesg snippet from p4-14-12: 
```
[    1.987654] nvidia: probe of 0000:3e:00.0 deferred
[    1.987660] nvidia: module tainted: GPU-priv
[   98.123456] nv-host: task hung; killing
[   98.123459] kernel: Out of memory: kill process 5812 (trainer) score 893
```
Also NCCL: "WARN Net/Plugin : handshake failed, timed out" in pod logs.

Connor: Autoscaler already started evicting pods. eu-west3 GPU pool lost ~20% immediate capacity (about 12 nodes). If we fallback to on-demand in-region cost projection is ~2.9x for the day. If we move traffic to eu-west1 reserved, we'll need tenant approvals for those pinned to eu-west3.

Tanya: Which driver/CUDA image was in use on those hosts? We built images with driver 535.104 and CUDA 12.1. Kernel compatibility was tested in CI but there were no heavy NCCL stress tests.

Maya: Confirmed 535 series. CI smoke passed but not full GPU stress. I'm going to PAUSE remaining kernel batches. deploy-bot: pause rollout?

deploy-bot: Kernel rollout to eu-west3 paused at 1943210045 by infra/rolling-upgrades (reason: probe failures). 25 hosts applied, 10 pending.

OpsOncall: Good. Immediate plan: 1) tag hosts failing probe with kernel-probe-failed-6.4 2) cordon + drain the worst 8 3) reimage pending hosts back to kernel 5.15 image 4) open support case with NVIDIA (attach nv-host dumps + dmesg + sysfs) 5) estimate customer impact and cost delta for on-demand.

Jin: Tagging/gcloud example:
```
# tag host
gcloud compute instances add-tags p4-14-12 --tags=kernel-probe-failed-6.4 --zone=europe-west3-c
```
I'll upload logs to gs://redwood-debug/eu-west3/1943210000/ (contains nv-host dump, dmesg, pod logs).

Connor: Dedicated/reserved pools: eu-west1 reserved has ~35% spare but a number of Dedicated customers explicitly require eu-west3. OpsOncall, can we provide a temporary exception to migrate non-regulated tenants?

OpsOncall: Yes for non-regulated. We'll need to notify tenants pinned to eu-west3. Ops to compile list and send comms. Reroute estimated time: 1.5-3 hours depending on DB reconfigs.

Tanya: Short-term mitigations to reduce impact on running jobs: bump NCCL handshake timeout and disable aggressive mem reclaim in user containers. Example envs to set in job templates: 
```
export NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS=2
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_TIMEOUT=900
```
Also enable driver fallback probe on the image (module.force_probe=true style) as a trial.

Maya: Action items I have: pause rollout (done), tag failed hosts, coordinate reimage of pending hosts to 5.15-image-2025-11-20-gpu-cuda12.1-rt, open NVIDIA ticket with attached logs, estimate on-demand cost and surface to finance. Who takes customer comms?

Connor: I'll draft the CS note and page account owners for any eu-west3-pinned Dedicated customers.

infra-bot: Alert: p4-14-12 failure rate > 2/hr, escalating to infra-sev at 1943210202.

Jin: Running a reproducer on a staging 3-node P4 cluster with kernel 6.4 + driver 535 to see if we can trigger NCCL handshake failure under scaled peer connects. Will post results.

OpsOncall: If reimage to 5.15 doesn't stabilize, we will do a package-level rollback for the kernel and add a stricter preflight NCCL probe to the rollout pipeline. For now: freeze upgrades, cordon & drain 8 worst hosts, reimage 10 pending to 5.15-image-2025-11-20, notify customers with pinned region, open NVIDIA support ticket. Update in 25m with logs and capacity numbers.
